implementation.method: Package trusted official prebuilt web/dist from the fixed-output v0.8.6 GitHub release archive; assert the separately pinned source fetch, committed package-lock digest, and reviewed cargo web build workflow step.
implementation.provenance: The fixed archive hash authenticates the downloaded bytes, and read-only Git/API checks confirm v0.8.6 resolves to the reviewed revision. These checks do not independently prove that the archive was built from that source or lockfile; the assets were not locally rebuilt or provenance-attested.
implementation.rationale: Upstream web builds first generate OpenAPI TypeScript from Rust, so a clean source-only npm build would violate the no-Rust-rebuild constraint. The reviewed release workflow specifies one web/dist build from the committed lockfile followed by reuse across architecture archives. Selecting the native x86_64 archive avoids ARM/QEMU work without changing the assets; x86_64 and aarch64 archive contents were independently compared byte-for-byte.

liveGateway.visualState: ZeroClaw pairing UI rendered correctly with logo, controls, and styling; no blank page or 503

integration: Instantiate with: zeroclawWeb = import ../packages/zeroclaw-web.nix { inherit pkgs; };
Set the generated ZeroClaw TOML value gateway.web_dist_dir to ${zeroclawWeb}/share/zeroclaw-web.
The Nix string reference keeps the assets in the system closure; no service, port, firewall, or binary-package change is required.
limitations: The GitHub release archive is a trusted official prebuilt input, not a locally rebuilt or independently provenance-attested artifact.
No deployment, SSH, reboot, service installation, firewall change, credentials, provider call, or pairing was performed.
The dashboard was accepted locally against the pinned production binary; deployed Pi acceptance remains the integrating worker's later gate.
